c.tagline: The Turkish Riviera's whitewashed jet-set port, where a Crusader castle guards a lively marina

card: Widely accepted at hotels, restaurants, and marina shops; small local eateries and beach clubs may prefer cash, so carry some Turkish lira.

taxi.fare: Roughly ₺30-50 flag fall plus metered per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard in town; agree a flat rate for trips to outlying peninsula villages like Gümüşlük or Türkbükü

emergency.note: 112 is Turkey's unified emergency number; private hospitals (e.g., Medical Park Bodrum) also serve tourists

religion: small Christian and other minority communities, particularly among the expat and tourist population
walk: Central Bodrum around the castle and marina is compact and walkable, with a lively bazaar and waterfront promenade; reaching outlying peninsula villages like Gümüşlük, Türkbükü, or Yalıkavak requires a dolmuş, taxi, or rental car.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers, including women; Bodrum is a well-established, cosmopolitan resort town popular with both Turkish and international visitors
safety.crime: Petty theft (unattended bags on beaches) is the main risk; violent crime against tourists is rare

hood_landmark.Bardakçı / Gümbet: Gümbet Beach's watersports and nightlife strip
hood_landmark.Gümüşlük: Ancient sunken city ruins and seafood harbor
hood_landmark.Türkbükü / Yalıkavak: Türkbükü's upscale beach clubs and Yalıkavak Marina

avoid.reason: Nightlife bill-padding and touts; jet-ski/rental scams

hood_desc: The historic heart of Bodrum town, anchored by the crusader castle and the bustling marina lined with cafes, boutiques, and yacht-charter offices.
A lively beach suburb just west of the center, known for watersports and Bodrum's most concentrated nightlife strip of bars and clubs.
A calmer, family-oriented beach town on the peninsula's south side, popular for its long sandy beach and windsurfing.
A picturesque fishing village on the peninsula's western tip, known for ancient sunken ruins visible in the clear water and relaxed seafood restaurants.
The peninsula's glamorous north-shore villages, home to designer boutiques, celebrity-favored beach clubs, and the upscale Yalıkavak Marina.
lodging: DoubleTree by Hilton Bodrum Marina Vista

water.note: Stick to bottled water, as locals do; tap water is not drunk here.

transit.sys: Dolmuş (shared minibus) network connecting Bodrum town to peninsula villages
transit.hours: Roughly 7am-midnight in high season, reduced off-season
transit.map: Dolmuş routes depart from the main Bodrum otogar (bus station) near the marina
transit.note: Ferries and water taxis also connect coastal villages around the peninsula in summer

transport.air: Milas-Bodrum Airport (BJV), about 35 km away, has direct flights from Istanbul and seasonal international routes from across Europe
transport.train: No direct rail service to Bodrum; the nearest major station is in Izmir
transport.bus: Overnight coaches connect Bodrum to Istanbul (~11-12 hrs), Izmir (~3.5 hrs), and other Turkish cities via the Bodrum otogar
transport.ferry: Seasonal ferries connect Bodrum to the Greek islands of Kos and Rhodes, and domestic ferries run to nearby coastal towns
transport.car: Self-driving is popular for exploring the peninsula's villages and coves; roads are well paved though narrow and winding on the outer peninsula

airport.name: Milas-Bodrum Airport
airport.transport: Havaş shuttle buses and pre-booked hotel transfers meet most flights; taxi transfer roughly $35-50

net.m: Excellent 4G/5G coverage throughout Bodrum and the peninsula, especially in high season
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels, cafes, and marina restaurants
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels, cafes, and beach clubs
net.ap: A Turkcell or Vodafone tourist SIM (sold at the airport with passport) or eSIM is recommended

tip.s: 10% is customary for hotel staff, boat captains, and tour guides
tip.r: 10% is standard at restaurants where service isn't already included

landmarks: Bodrum Castle (Castle of St. Peter)
Built by Crusader knights in the fifteenth century, this harbor fortress now houses the world-class Museum of Underwater Archaeology and its ancient shipwreck treasures.
Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
The scattered foundations of King Mausolus's monumental tomb, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, still whisper of Halicarnassus's fourth-century-BC glory.
Ancient Theatre of Halicarnassus
Carved into the hillside above town in the fourth century BC, this 13,000-seat theatre frames sublime views over Bodrum's bay and castle.
Myndos Gate
The restored western gate of Halicarnassus's ancient walls marks where Alexander the Great besieged the city in 334 BC, flanked by moat remains.
Bodrum Windmills
A ridge of ruined whitewashed windmills from the eighteenth century separates Bodrum's two bays, a favorite sunset spot overlooking castle, marina and Aegean.
Bodrum Marina and Bar Street
Gleaming gulets and superyachts line the palm-fringed marina, spilling into whitewashed lanes of boutiques, fish restaurants and the famous nightlife of Cumhuriyet Caddesi.
Gümüşlük (Ancient Myndos)
A bohemian fishing village atop ancient Myndos, where diners eat fresh fish at water's edge and wade to Rabbit Island over submerged ruins.
Zeki Müren Arts Museum
The flamboyant villa of Turkey's most beloved singer preserves his sequined stage costumes and paintings, an intimate portrait of the 'Sun of Art'.
Kara Ada (Black Island)
Daily boat trips cross to this pine-covered island whose therapeutic hot springs and orange-tinted mud baths bubble straight into the sea.
Bodrum Maritime Museum
Model gulets and a renowned seashell collection celebrate Bodrum's sponge-diving and boat-building heritage, honoring writer-fisherman Cevat Şakir, the 'Fisherman of Halicarnassus'.

train.note: There is no railway on the Bodrum peninsula. The nearest TCDD station is at Denizli, roughly 4 hours inland, on the İzmir regional line. Most visitors fly into Bodrum-Milas airport or arrive by coach.

bus.note: No international coaches. Bodrum's otogar is central, with frequent services to İzmir (about 3h30), Marmaris, Fethiye, Pamukkale and overnight coaches to Istanbul and Ankara on Pamukkale (https://www.pamukkale.com.tr/) and Kamil Koç (https://www.kamilkoc.com.tr/). Book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/). Dolmuş minibuses cover Gümbet, Bitez, Yalıkavak and the rest of the peninsula.

intl.op: Bodrum Ferryboat / Bodrum Express Lines — tickets at the harbour ticket offices

ferry.note: The Kos crossing is the workhorse - about 20 minutes from Bodrum's harbour, several sailings a day in summer and a much thinner winter timetable. Rhodes runs seasonally and takes far longer. All of these are proper border crossings, so bring your passport and arrive an hour early. The Datça ferry across the gulf saves a long drive around the peninsula.

half.name: Kos
half.blurb: Greek island a one-hour ferry away, with a medieval Knights Hospitaller castle, cobbled lanes and a laid-back harbor town.

half.name: Datça Peninsula
half.blurb: Quiet peninsula of pine forests and secluded coves southwest of Bodrum, known for its slower pace and almond orchards.

full.name: Pamukkale
full.blurb: Cotton-white travertine terraces of mineral pools beside the Roman ruins of Hierapolis, one of Turkey's most photographed natural sites.

full.name: Ephesus (Selçuk)
full.blurb: Best-preserved ancient Greco-Roman city in the Mediterranean, with the Library of Celsus and a 25,000-seat amphitheater still standing.
